title: harness-runner-compatibility-and-sample-profile-seeding
creator: Sophia Ramirez
description: Problem: The current benchmark harness produces performance profiles with high run-to-run variance and has brittle integrations for heterogeneous eval runners (streaming, sync, external service runners). This makes automated model onboarding and stable version pinning unreliable. Goal: Extend the harness to provide a repeatable profile-seeding flow that (1) adapts to multiple runner interfaces via pluggable adapters, (2) deterministically samples datasets and prompt variants with fingerprinting, and (3) emits a publishable profile artifact (JSON) containing key metrics, dataset/prompt fingerprints, hardware/runtime fingerprints and metadata suitable for version pinning and downstream routing policies. This ticket implements the core library pieces, CI integration, and a docs page for the onboarding flow.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness exposes runner adapter interface supporting: sync-step runners, streaming-token runners, and external HTTP runners. 2) Deterministic dataset sampler implemented: given seed + dataset fingerprint -> same sample subset and order across runs. 3) Prompt variant registry: stores canonical variants and weights; sampling deterministic. 4) Generated profile JSON contains: model_name, model_version, runtime_signature (kernel set + quantization), hardware_fingerprint, dataset_fingerprints, prompt_variant_ids, per-scenario metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens/s, quality score), and overall summary. 5) Round-trip reproducibility test: re-run on CI twice within identical infra config -> key metrics CV < 3%. 6) End-to-end demo: onboard an internal Llama-variant and publish profile to staging S3 path. 7) Confluence doc + example GitHub Actions workflow merged.
plan: Design (2d): review existing harness contracts and define a minimal runner-adapter API (execute(), stream(), healthcheck()). Implementation (6d):  - adapter layer with three concrete adapters (sync/mock runner, streaming-local runner, http-external runner).  - deterministic sampler: implement fingerprinting using SHA256 over dataset metadata + canonical order; sampling uses keyed RNG (xoroshiro or PCG) with explicit seed parameter.  - prompt registry: proto format + migrations; include tooling to produce variant IDs and weights.  - profile writer: produce stable JSON schema v1.0 and upload to staging S3. Testing (3d): unit tests for adapters, sampler determinism tests, integration test that runs small profile and validates schema. CI (1d): GitHub Action to run a lightweight profile on PRs for release branch. Docs (1d): onboarding guide and example. Rollout: merge behind feature flag and enable for internal onboarding flows, then enable for partner onboarding after 1 week of internal validation.
risks: 1) Hardware variance across CI runners reduces reproducibility; mitigations: pin instance types, record hardware_fingerprint and report CVs. 2) Large datasets increase runtime/cost; mitigations: default to small probes and provide config for full runs. 3) External runner timeouts / contract drift; mitigations: strict healthcheck and versioned adapter shim. 4) Dataset licensing – cannot publish raw samples; only publish dataset fingerprint and stats in profile. 5) Schema evolution compatibility – include version field and migration notes.
metrics: - reproducibility_cv_threshold: <3% for latency p50/p95 across repeated runs on same infra. - profile_generation_time_target: <30m for medium probe (10k tokens total). - storage_per_profile: <500KB compressed. - CI lightweight-run_time: <10m. - adoption: number of models onboarded with new profiles in first 30 days.
